title: Review of SkillsFuture Framework and Costs of Courses to Better Support Upskilling and Reskilling
what_it_is: Review of SkillsFuture Framework and Costs of Courses to Better Support Upskilling and Reskilling

sections.label: SkillsFuture support for PMETs
sections.summary: The passage sets out SkillsFuture subsidies, credits and a training allowance supporting PMETs and mid-career Singaporeans aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry will consider reviewing the SkillsFuture framework to better support professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) given feedback that some upskilling and reskilling programmes may cost more than existing SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: This includes course fee subsidies of up to 70%, as well as an opening SkillsFuture Credit of $500 at the age of 25.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: These Credits can be used to offset the remaining out-of-pocket costs for a range of training programmes, such as shorter standalone courses, SkillsFuture Career Transition Programmes, as well as full qualifications and stackable micro-credentials delivered by the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Additional support is given to mid-career Singaporeans aged 40 and above, as we recognise that they may require a substantive skills reboot, having completed their work-ready qualifications many years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Hence, Singaporeans aged 40 and above enjoy the Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy, which increases the course fee subsidy to up to 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: They also receive a $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up, which can be used for a curated set of substantive training courses that have better employability outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: This $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) is generally sufficient to offset the out-of-pocket course fees for a part-time or post-diploma and most SkillsFuture Career Transition Programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: A training allowance, computed at 50% of one's average income over the most recent 12 months and capped at $3,000 per month, is also given to partially offset income loss when they undergo long-form training.

sections.label: Reviewing reskilling support
sections.summary: The passage states that courses and support for training providers, employers and trainees are regularly reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, we are regularly reviewing the courses and the way in which we support both the training providers, the employers and trainees to reskill and upskill.

sections.label: Openness to reviewing SkillsFuture
sections.summary: The passage states the SkillsFuture structure supports all Singaporeans and that reviewing courses and training delivery is open.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, the overall structure of SkillsFuture, the way in which we support and subsidise the training providers, as well as the trainees, the Singaporeans, through the credits and subsidies, is very much along the lines that he described, not just for those with very specialised skills, but for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And if this means that for some certain situations we have to look at the courses that are available, the training processes that we deliver in partnership with employers, as well as the IHLs and training providers, we are certainly open to reviewing how we do so.
